source: hand-computed from the clause 4.1.2 and 4.1.4 field layouts
note: USLP transfer frames. The primary header is variable length: the End of Frame Primary Header flag selects a 4-octet truncated header, otherwise the header runs to 7 octets plus the VCF count field, whose length the 3-bit VCF Count Length field gives. That variability is why each form is pinned separately — a decoder that picks the wrong header size shifts every field after it.

encode.name: non-truncated-with-vcf-count-and-crc16
encode.note: TFVN '1100', SCID 1234 (0x04d2), source/dest 1, VCID 42, MAP ID 5, EOFPH 0, frame length 18-1 = 17, bypass 0, protocol control 0, OCF flag 0, VCF count length 2, VCF count 258. byte 0 = 1100 | scid[15:12] = 0xc0; byte 1 = scid[11:4] = 0x4d; byte 2 = scid[3:0]|S/D|vcid[5:3] = 0x2d; byte 3 = vcid[2:0]|mapid|eofph = 0x4a; bytes 4-5 = frame length 0x0011; byte 6 = 0x02 (VCF count length 2); bytes 7-8 = VCF count 0x0102. TFDF header 0x00 is construction rule '000' with UPID 0, then the 2-octet pointer 0x0000, then the data zone deadbeef. FECF is CRC-16-CCITT over everything before it = 0x0e51, recomputed independently.

encode.name: truncated-frame
encode.note: The End of Frame Primary Header flag makes the header 4 octets and drops the frame length, flags and VCF count entirely: a truncated frame's length is known from the channel, not the frame. SCID 0xab, VCID 1, MAP ID 2, EOFPH 1. byte 3 = vcid[2:0]<<5 | mapid<<1 | 1 = 0x25. Then the TFDF header 0xe5 (construction rule '111', UPID 5) and the data zone 112233. No FECF on this channel.

encode.name: with-ocf-and-crc16
encode.note: SCID 100, VCID 1, MAP 0, no VCF count, construction rule '111' with UPID 0, data zone 0102, OCF aabbccdd, 16-bit FECF. The OCF flag is bit 52, so byte 6 = 0x08. Total 16 octets means a frame length field of 15 (0x000f). The FECF is the last 16 bits of the frame, after the OCF, giving 0x778e. The OCF is located from the in-band flag, not from channel configuration.

encode.name: oid-pn-fill-sequence-twenty-octets
encode.note: The mandatory Only Idle Data fill generator: a 32-cell Fibonacci LFSR seeded all ones. CCSDS 732.1-B-3 annex H prints the stream verbatim: FF FF FF FF 6D B6 D8 61 45 1F 11 F1 97 16 72 3C BE 7E 00 B1. Transcribed from those published digits. Cross-check: the first ten octets are identical to the oid-sequence-first-ten-octets vector in vectors/pn/sequences.json, which CCSDS 132.0-B-3 publishes independently for TM — two standards printing the same stream.

decode.name: non-truncated-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of non-truncated-with-vcf-count-and-crc16. Every variable-length-header field must come back, including the VCF count whose width the header itself declares. The TFDF header is also read back: construction rule '000' carries a 16-bit pointer (clause 4.1.4.2.4.1), which is the First Header Pointer here.

decode.name: truncated-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of truncated-frame. The EOFPH flag must be read before anything after byte 3 is interpreted, so a decoder that reads the frame length first fails here. Construction rule '111' carries no pointer field, so the data zone starts immediately after the TFDF header octet.

decode.name: ocf-recovered-from-the-in-band-flag
decode.note: The inverse of with-ocf-and-crc16. The OCF is located from the OCF flag in the header, not from channel configuration.

reject.name: frame-length-field-disagrees-with-the-octets-present
reject.note: The frame length field says 17 (total 18 octets) but the frame is shorter. USLP carries its own length, so a decoder must cross-check it rather than trusting the buffer it was handed.

reject.name: header-truncated-below-four-octets
reject.note: Even the truncated header form needs four octets. A decoder must not get past octet 2: even a truncated primary header is 4 octets; the input stops after 2.

reject.name: source-or-dest-flag-above-one-bit-field
reject.note: The source-or-destination flag is one bit, so only 0 and 1 are meaningful. A wider value must be refused rather than masked, because masking 2 to 0 flips the frame's meaning from destination to source without saying so.

reject.name: map-id-above-four-bit-field
reject.note: 16 does not fit the 4-bit MAP ID field. It must be refused rather than masked: masking would deliver the frame to a different multiplexer access point than the caller named.

reject.name: virtual-channel-id-above-six-bit-field
reject.note: 64 does not fit the 6-bit VCID field. It must be refused rather than masked: masking would route the frame to a different virtual channel than the caller named.
